title: Getting to the Dooars: Trains, Buses and Cars
meta_description: How to reach the Dooars from NJP, Bagdogra and Siliguri: Dooars line trains to New Mal Jn, Hasimara and Alipurduar, NBSTC buses, reserved car fares.
summary: Reach the Dooars from New Jalpaiguri (NJP) station, Bagdogra airport or Siliguri. Reserved cars cost ₹3,000–3,800 to Lataguri and ₹4,000–5,000 to Madarihat. Buses from Siliguri's Tenzing Norgay terminus run east for ₹100–300. The cheapest route is the Dooars line railway to New Mal Junction, Chalsa, Madarihat, Hasimara and Alipurduar.

sections.heading: The gateways: NJP, Bagdogra and Siliguri
paras: Everything starts at Siliguri, the town on the narrow Siliguri Corridor where roads and railways from the rest of India meet those of the Northeast. New Jalpaiguri (NJP) is the main railhead, about 6 km from the town centre, with direct trains from Kolkata, Delhi, Guwahati, Patna, Mumbai and Bengaluru. Bagdogra airport (IXB), 12–15 km west of Siliguri, has flights from Kolkata, Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Chennai and other cities. Siliguri Junction, near the bus terminus, handles some of the Dooars line trains.

The Dooars spread east from here for about 200 km along the foot of the hills, from the Teesta to the Sankosh. Lataguri and Murti, the bases for Gorumara, are 75–90 km away; Madarihat, for Jaldapara, about 125 km; Alipurduar about 160 km; Jayanti and the Buxa road head at Santalabari about 180–190 km. Most visitors travel east along the line of parks and back, or enter from Siliguri and leave from Alipurduar, which has its own trains to Kolkata.

sections.heading: By train on the Dooars line
paras: The Dooars line is the railway that runs from Siliguri and NJP east along the foothills to Alipurduar, first built as the Bengal Dooars Railway in the 1890s to carry tea. It crosses the Teesta at Sevoke, then runs through Bagrakote, Oodlabari, Damdim and New Mal Junction in Malbazar, climbs gently to Chalsa, crosses the forest between Gorumara and Chapramari, and continues past Nagrakata, Banarhat, Binnaguri, Birpara, Madarihat, Hasimara, Hamiltonganj and Rajabhatkhawa to Alipurduar Junction. For long stretches tea gardens and sal forest come right up to the track.

The line is single-track and services are few, perhaps a handful each way a day, including express trains from Kolkata such as the Kanchankanya Express from Sealdah, and local passenger and intercity services from Siliguri and NJP. Journeys are slow by road standards: about two to two and a half hours from NJP to New Mal Junction, and four to five hours to Hasimara or Alipurduar. Fares are low, ₹40–450 depending on class. Trains slow down in forest sections because elephants cross the line, and accidents here have killed elephants, most notoriously near Chapramari in 2013.
Timetables change, new services are added and others suspended, so check the current timetable on the Indian Railways site or app before you plan a day around a train.

sections.heading: By bus from Siliguri
paras: Buses leave from the Tenzing Norgay Central Bus Terminus on Hill Cart Road in Siliguri, run by North Bengal State Transport Corporation (NBSTC) and private operators. Buses towards Malbazar, Maynaguri, Birpara, Alipurduar, Falakata and Cooch Behar run through the day, more often in the morning. Fares are ₹100–150 to Lataguri or Malbazar, ₹150–250 to Madarihat and ₹200–300 to Alipurduar.

Buses for Lataguri usually take the route via Jalpaiguri and Maynaguri, or via Sevoke and Malbazar, and drop you on the highway in about three hours; tell the conductor where you want to get off. Buses to Madarihat take about five hours via Malbazar, Chalsa and Birpara. They are crowded, sometimes slow and very cheap. Luggage goes on the roof or under your feet, so travel light. Overnight NBSTC and private buses also run from Kolkata's Esplanade to Siliguri, Alipurduar and Cooch Behar.

sections.heading: By reserved car or shared jeep
paras: A reserved car is the fastest option, and with four people sharing it is not much more expensive than the train plus local transfers. Prepaid counters at Bagdogra and taxi stands at NJP and Siliguri quote by destination. Small cars cost less than SUVs; drivers expect a tip and you pay for their return trip. These are indicative 2025–26 fares for a small car.
list: NJP or Bagdogra to Lataguri or Murti: ₹3,000–3,800, 2–2.5 hours
NJP to Samsing or Suntalekhola: ₹3,500–4,500, about 3 hours
NJP to Jhalong or Bindu: ₹4,000–5,500, 3–4 hours
NJP to Madarihat for Jaldapara: ₹4,000–5,000, about 4 hours
NJP to Jayanti or Santalabari for Buxa: ₹5,500–6,500, about 5 hours

sections.heading: Moving between the parks
paras: Shared jeeps are a hill habit and only partly useful here. They run up the side valleys from the Chalsa and Metali area to Samsing and towards Jhalong and Bindu, mostly in the morning and leaving when full, for ₹40–150 a seat. In the plains you will use buses, autos and the train instead.

Gorumara, Jaldapara and Buxa sit in a line along the foothills, so the most efficient trip moves east without doubling back. A common plan is two nights at Lataguri or Murti for Gorumara and Chapramari, a train or car to Madarihat for two nights at Jaldapara, and, with more time, a night at Chilapata and two at Buxa or Jayanti before leaving from Alipurduar. Detours to Samsing and Jhalong are easiest from Murti or Chalsa.

Roads in the region have improved, but the National Highway between Siliguri and Assam carries heavy truck traffic, and some forest stretches have speed limits for wildlife. Driving after dark through forest roads is discouraged; elephants cross often and drivers prefer to finish before dusk.

sections.heading: Three ways in, from cheapest to quickest
paras: Here is how the same first day looks for three different budgets, starting with a morning arrival at NJP and ending at a Lataguri homestay in time for an afternoon Gorumara safari.

The cheapest: take an auto from NJP to Siliguri Junction or stay at NJP for a Dooars line train to New Mal Junction, ₹40–150 in an unreserved or second class seat, then an auto or shared car to Lataguri for ₹400–600 for the vehicle. Total for two people, around ₹700–900, and about four hours with waiting. It depends entirely on a train that suits your arrival, so check the timetable first.

The middle way: an auto from NJP to the Tenzing Norgay bus terminus, ₹200–300 reserved, then a bus to Lataguri for ₹100–150 each. Total for two, around ₹500–600, and four to five hours door to door. Buses run more often than trains, which makes this the most flexible budget option.

The quickest: a small reserved car from NJP or Bagdogra straight to your homestay, ₹3,000–3,800 for up to four people, about two hours. If you land at Bagdogra after noon, this is usually the only way to reach the afternoon safari slot.

sections.heading: Bhutan, Assam and onward travel
paras: Hasimara is about 20 km from Jaigaon, the Indian border town opposite Phuentsholing in Bhutan. Travellers who want to visit Bhutan cross here with the documents, permits and fees that Bhutan currently requires; rules for Indian nationals have changed several times in recent years. There is no crossing for travellers at Jhalong, Bindu, Buxa or Jayanti, even where Bhutan is across the river. For Assam, the main line trains from New Alipurduar and New Cooch Behar continue to Guwahati. Check current status before you travel.

Leaving the Dooars, you do not have to go back to Siliguri. Alipurduar Junction and New Alipurduar have direct trains to Kolkata, and the Kanchankanya Express runs back to Sealdah along the Dooars line itself. Cooch Behar, with its palace and temples, is about an hour south of Alipurduar by bus. If you are flying out of Bagdogra, allow a full day from Jayanti or Buxa, or break the journey with a night in Madarihat or Lataguri.

faqs.q: What is the nearest railway station to Gorumara?
faqs.a: New Mal Junction in Malbazar, about 15 km from Lataguri, is the nearest station on the Dooars line, about two to two and a half hours from NJP. Chalsa is closer to Murti and Chapramari. Many travellers arrive at NJP and take a reserved car to Lataguri for ₹3,000–3,800, which takes about two hours.

faqs.q: What is the nearest station to Jaldapara?
faqs.a: Madarihat station is in the town that serves as Jaldapara's base, and Hasimara is about 10–15 km away near Chilapata. Both are on the Dooars line, four to five hours from NJP or Siliguri Junction. Check the current timetable, then take an auto or car to your lodge for ₹50–500.

faqs.q: How do we get from Siliguri to the Dooars by bus?
faqs.a: From the Tenzing Norgay Central Bus Terminus on Hill Cart Road. NBSTC and private buses run towards Malbazar, Maynaguri, Birpara and Alipurduar through the day. Fares are about ₹100–150 to Lataguri, ₹150–250 to Madarihat and ₹200–300 to Alipurduar. Tell the conductor your stop, as Lataguri is a highway halt.

faqs.q: How much is a taxi from Bagdogra to Lataguri?
faqs.a: About ₹3,000–3,800 for a small car from the prepaid counter or a taxi stand, indicative for 2025–26, and the drive takes two to two and a half hours via Sevoke and Malbazar. SUVs cost more. Agree whether tolls and parking are included before you set off.

faqs.q: Is the Dooars train journey scenic?
faqs.a: Yes. After crossing the Teesta at Sevoke, the Dooars line runs through tea gardens and sal forest for long stretches, with the hills on your left heading east. The section between Chalsa and Nagrakata passes between Gorumara and Chapramari. Sit on the north side, and travel by day.

faqs.q: Which station is best for Buxa Fort?
faqs.a: Rajabhatkhawa, about 15 km from Santalabari where the walk to the fort begins, or Alipurduar Junction, about 30 km away, which has more trains. From Rajabhatkhawa take a local car for ₹600–1,000. Check the current timetable, as few trains stop at the smaller stations.

faqs.q: How do we travel from Gorumara to Jaldapara?
faqs.a: By train from New Mal Junction or Chalsa to Madarihat, about two hours and very cheap, with autos or cars at each end. Or by bus via Birpara, or by reserved car from Lataguri for ₹3,000–3,500, which takes two to two and a half hours over about 80–90 km.

faqs.q: Can we enter Bhutan from the Dooars?
faqs.a: Yes, through Jaigaon and Phuentsholing, about 20 km from Hasimara, with the documents, permits and fees Bhutan currently requires. There is no crossing for travellers at Jhalong, Bindu, Buxa or Jayanti. Rules for Indian and foreign nationals have changed in recent years; check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Is it safe to drive at night in the Dooars?
faqs.a: It is best avoided. Forest stretches of road near Gorumara, Chapramari, Jaldapara and Buxa are elephant crossings, and drivers prefer to finish before dusk. Highways also carry heavy trucks at night. Plan transfers for daylight, and if you arrive late at NJP, sleep in Siliguri and leave early.
